Chapter 7: Healing Old Wounds and Making Peace with the Past
Have you ever noticed how some memories just won’t let go? It’s like, no matter how much time passes, those old wounds—maybe something someone said in anger, or that moment you felt rejected, or even a failure that still stings—they can feel like they’re holding you back. Almost like anchors, stopping you from really believing in your own worth.
But here’s the thing: healing those wounds... it’s possible. It’s not quick, and it’s definitely not easy. But you can do it.
Let me share a story. There was a man who spent years living under the shadow of his father’s disappointment. Every time he achieved something, it felt empty. Every mistake? It just seemed to prove his worst fears. Then, after a tough conversation, he realized he was still chasing approval he might never get. The pain was so real. But so was the hope that he could finally let go.
He started writing letters he never planned to send, pouring out everything he hadn’t been able to say. He talked things through with a counselor, naming the hurt and actually allowing himself to grieve. And slowly—really, step by step—the grip of those memories started to loosen. They never fully disappeared, but they stopped defining who he was.
There’s another story—a woman who couldn’t forgive herself after a friendship ended badly. She kept replaying every conversation, every mistake, convinced she didn’t deserve to be loved. But when she finally opened up to a trusted friend, something changed. Instead of judgment, she found compassion. Just being seen, flaws and all, became a turning point. She realized forgiveness, for others and for herself, was a gift she could choose to accept.
You know, most of us carry wounds that shape the way we see ourselves. Some are obvious, but others—they’re hidden under layers of staying busy or just trying to ignore the pain. Healing really starts with honesty. It takes courage to face what hurts instead of running from it. It means allowing yourself to feel that grief, the anger, all those emotions you’ve tried to bury.
But here’s something important—healing also means making a choice to let go of the past. That doesn’t mean you forget, or that what happened didn’t matter. It just means you refuse to let old wounds decide your future. For a lot of people, faith becomes a huge comfort. It’s a reminder that nothing is beyond redemption, that even the deepest scars can turn into places where you grow.
And remember, this process isn’t a straight line. There’ll be days when the pain comes back, when those old stories feel true all over again. But with each step, the past loses a little more power. Most people find that, once they make peace with what happened, they can finally embrace what’s here and now—and move forward, feeling lighter than they ever thought possible.
